subject.title: [security] exe.dev stop can delete VMs that Crabbox cannot prove it owns

question: Should exe-dev destructive release reject name, normalized-name, and SSH-host matches unless a local claim or matching Crabbox ownership tags prove the VM belongs to the lease?
rationale: The security docs and VISION.md support fail-closed ownership checks, but current exe-dev stop docs expose raw VM-name deletion, so maintainers need to own the security boundary and compatibility decision.

options.title: Fail Closed On Unproven Targets
options.body: Require an exact local claim or matching Crabbox tags before `exe.dev rm`, then update docs and tests around the stricter destructive boundary.

options.title: Add Explicit Adoption First
options.body: Preserve a raw-identifier workflow only through an explicit reclaim/adoption step that stores the verified binding before deletion.

options.title: Keep Legacy Raw Deletion
options.body: Continue allowing claimless VM-name deletion and accept the provider-resource ownership risk as documented behavior.

recommendation.title: Fail Closed On Unproven Targets
recommendation.body: Require an exact local claim or matching Crabbox tags before `exe.dev rm`, then update docs and tests around the stricter destructive boundary.
